lesson.title: Asking for Help and Making Introductions
lesson.subtitle: Polite requests and helpful answers
lesson.description: Ask for assistance, apologize politely, introduce a friend and pass along information.

learning_objectives: Ask for help politely with 帮忙 (bāngmáng).
Use 不好意思 (bù hǎoyìsi) before an interruption or apology.
Introduce others and relay simple information.

metadata.audience: HSK 3.0 Level 2 learners with Level 1 foundations

overview.topic_description: Ask for assistance, apologize politely, introduce a friend and pass along information.
overview.focus: Ask for help politely with 帮忙 (bāngmáng).

items.meaning_en: to help; to do a favor

examples.pinyin: nǐ néng bāngmáng ma?
examples.english: Can you help?
examples.teaching_note: A short spoken example using 帮忙.

examples.hanzi: 有问题的时候，可以请老师帮忙。
examples.pinyin: yǒu wèntí de shíhou, kěyǐ qǐng lǎoshī bāngmáng.
examples.english: When there is a problem, you can ask the teacher for help.
examples.teaching_note: A simple written example using 帮忙.

examples.pinyin: bù hǎoyìsi, wǒ lái wǎn le.
examples.english: Sorry, I'm late.
examples.teaching_note: A short spoken example using 不好意思.

examples.hanzi: “不好意思，这里有人坐吗？”他问。
examples.pinyin: “bù hǎoyìsi, zhèlǐ yǒu rén zuò ma?” tā wèn.
examples.english: "Excuse me, is anyone sitting here?" he asked.
examples.teaching_note: A simple written example using 不好意思.

examples.pinyin: qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐ de míngzi.
examples.english: Please tell me your name.
examples.teaching_note: A short spoken example using 告诉.

examples.hanzi: 老师告诉学生明天有考试。
examples.pinyin: lǎoshī gàosu xuéshēng míngtiān yǒu kǎoshì.
examples.english: The teacher told the students there would be a test tomorrow.
examples.teaching_note: A simple written example using 告诉.

examples.pinyin: nǐ néng jièshào yíxià zìjǐ ma?
examples.english: Can you introduce yourself briefly?
examples.teaching_note: A short spoken example using 介绍.

examples.hanzi: 老师介绍了一位新同学。
examples.pinyin: lǎoshī jièshào le yí wèi xīn tóngxué.
examples.english: The teacher introduced a new classmate.
examples.teaching_note: A simple written example using 介绍.

items.meaning_en: to let; to ask; to make (someone do something)

examples.pinyin: ràng wǒ kànkan.
examples.english: Let me have a look.
examples.teaching_note: A short spoken example using 让.

examples.pinyin: lǎoshī ràng xuéshēng dǎkāi shū.
examples.english: The teacher asks the students to open their books.
examples.teaching_note: A simple written example using 让.

examples.pinyin: nǐ xiào shénme?
examples.english: What are you laughing at?
examples.teaching_note: A short spoken example using 笑.

examples.pinyin: lǎoshī xiào zhe gēn xuéshēng shuōhuà.
examples.english: The teacher speaks to the students with a smile.
examples.teaching_note: A simple written example using 笑.

examples.pinyin: bú kèqi!
examples.english: You're welcome!
examples.teaching_note: 不客气 is a standard spoken response to thanks; the short answer is a complete utterance.

examples.pinyin: tā shuō: “bú kèqi.”
examples.english: She said, "You're welcome."
examples.teaching_note: Written dialogue: 不客气 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.

items.pos_note: Conventional response to thanks; classify as a fixed expression, not by the characters separately.

examples.pinyin: wǒ yào gěi māma dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: I want to call my mother.
examples.teaching_note: 给妈妈 identifies the recipient of the phone call; 打电话 is a verb-object expression.

examples.hanzi: 请明天上午给老师打电话。
examples.pinyin: qǐng míngtiān shàngwǔ gěi lǎoshī dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: Please call the teacher tomorrow morning.
examples.teaching_note: Short everyday instruction or request using 打电话; the tone is polite or neutral.

examples.pinyin: duìbuqǐ, wǒ lái wǎn le.
examples.english: Sorry, I came late.
examples.teaching_note: 对不起 is an apology; 来晚了 means arriving late, with 了 indicating the completed situation.

examples.pinyin: “duìbuqǐ, wǒ méiyǒu kànjiàn nǐ.” tā shuō.
examples.english: "I'm sorry, I didn't see you," she said.
examples.teaching_note: Written dialogue: 对不起 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.

items.pos_note: Conventional apology; can be analyzed as a verb phrase, but functions as a fixed social expression.

grammar_points.title: Making a polite request
grammar_points.explanation: Use 不好意思 (bù hǎoyìsi) as a polite opening, then ask someone to 帮忙 (bāngmáng) or 帮 (bāng) you with a specific action.

grammar_points.title: Telling and introducing
grammar_points.explanation: 告诉 (gàosu) introduces information shared with someone, while 介绍 (jièshào) introduces a person or explains something to someone.

questions.prompt: What is happening in the second part of the reading?
questions.explanation: Use the details in the second paragraph to justify your answer.
questions.answer: The teacher asks Xiao Li to introduce the new classmate. Everyone laughs because the newcomer speaks amusingly.

questions.prompt: Write the Mandarin sentence for: Please help me carry this bag. Give both Hanzi and pinyin.
questions.explanation: Use the expressions and grammar you have practised. Suggested answer: 请帮我拿一下这个包。 (Qǐng bāng wǒ ná yíxià zhè ge bāo.)
questions.answer: 请帮我拿一下这个包。 (Qǐng bāng wǒ ná yíxià zhè ge bāo.)

dialogue.title: Asking for Help and Making Introductions
dialogue.context_en: Ask for assistance, apologize politely, introduce a friend and pass along information.

turns.speaker: A
turns.hanzi: 不好意思，你能帮我一个忙吗？
turns.pinyin: Bù hǎoyìsi, nǐ néng bāng wǒ yí ge máng ma?
turns.english: Excuse me, can you help me with something?

turns.speaker: B
turns.hanzi: 当然可以！你想让我做什么？
turns.pinyin: Dāngrán kěyǐ! Nǐ xiǎng ràng wǒ zuò shénme?
turns.english: Of course! What would you like me to do?

turns.speaker: A
turns.pinyin: Qǐng gàosu wǒ jiàoshì zài nǎr.
turns.english: Please tell me where the classroom is.

turns.speaker: B
turns.hanzi: 我带你去，还可以介绍我的朋友。
turns.pinyin: Wǒ dài nǐ qù, hái kěyǐ jièshào wǒ de péngyou.
turns.english: I will take you there and can introduce my friend too.

reading.title: Asking for Help and Making Introductions — short reading

paragraphs.hanzi: 小张第一次来学校，不知道教室在哪儿。小李主动来帮忙。
paragraphs.pinyin: Xiǎo Zhāng dì yī cì lái xuéxiào, bù zhīdào jiàoshì zài nǎr. Xiǎo Lǐ zhǔdòng lái bāngmáng.
paragraphs.english: Xiao Zhang is at school for the first time and does not know where the classroom is. Xiao Li offers to help.

paragraphs.hanzi: 老师让小李介绍新同学。大家听了以后都笑了，因为新同学说话很有意思。
paragraphs.pinyin: Lǎoshī ràng Xiǎo Lǐ jièshào xīn tóngxué. Dàjiā tīng le yǐhòu dōu xiào le, yīnwèi xīn tóngxué shuōhuà hěn yǒu yìsi.
paragraphs.english: The teacher asks Xiao Li to introduce the new classmate. Everyone laughs because the newcomer speaks amusingly.

teaching_plan.common_pitfall: 帮忙 (bāngmáng) commonly means lend a hand; 帮 (bāng) can take a person and the action directly. Keep the person and requested action clear.
teaching_plan.pronunciation_focus: Practise the neutral ending of 告诉 (gàosu) and the fourth tone in 介绍 (jièshào).
